# flyee.club — Platform monorepo

The PLATFORM of flyee.club: accounts, billing (Asaas for BRL, Stripe for USD), entitlements, member token issuance with 30-day revalidation, the package-delivery API the `npx flyee` CLI consumes, catalog and release management, the member dashboard, admin consoles, per-segment metrics, the waitlist and the bilingual public site. The PRODUCT (the CLI, the harness core and the module contents) is a separate project that consumes this platform's API contract and module manifest; it never lives here. This repo has no link to any template: it was copied from the MedChina codebase on 2026-09-30 and is being reshaped into the platform phase by phase.

## Where things stand

- Plan and progress: `docs/PLANO-IMPLEMENTACAO.md` (phases 0–8; the "Andamento" table says what is done). Product decisions and open questions: `docs/PRODUCT.md`.
- Done: phase 0 (identity, two locales, de-templated harness), phase 1 (clinical code, mobile app and dead packages removed), phase 2 (the database baseline), phase 7.1 (path-based locales for the public site), the code of the first-deploy milestone (bilingual waitlist with double opt-in, legal pages from `consent_terms`, launch stage and company line managed at `/admin/support`), phase 4 (the billing ladder: kit, membership and Pro, in BRL through Asaas and USD through Stripe, `docs/BILLING.md`) and phase 3 (the CLI token server, the `/api/cli/*` delivery API, the module manifest and the package upload, `docs/CLI-CONTRACT.md`). The deploy itself waits on the new services and the company data (`docs/DEPLOY.md`, "Primeiro deploy"). Next: phase 5, the member dashboard.
- **The database is the flyee.club baseline** (`packages/db/migrations`, `0000`–`0018`, plus `0019_launch` on top, with the pgTAP suite in `packages/db/tests`). It has not been applied to a hosted project yet: that happens once the new Supabase project exists (`npm run db:gate:remote`). New schema work is a new numbered migration on top of it. See `packages/db/README.md`.

## Safety during the transition

- `apps/web/.env` is inherited and holds **MedChina production credentials** (Supabase, Asaas, Meta, GA4, AI keys). `apps/web/.env.local` blanks every one of them and must stay in place until the new flyee.club services exist. Next.js loads `.env.local` first, so the blank wins.
- Never run `db:plan:remote`, `db:migrate:remote`, `db:gate:remote` or `test:db:remote` until `.env.local` points at the new flyee.club Supabase project. The gate (`scripts/remote-db-gate.mjs`) reads `.env.local` first, bootstraps an EMPTY project, and refuses a database it did not build (the MedChina one included, whose history names files this repo does not have), but do not lean on that.
- Never commit `.env` or `.env.local`. Commit per plan phase, never push without being asked.

## Product (summary of docs/PRODUCT.md)

- **What it is**: a club sold as a one-time entry kit plus a subscription. Members install the flyee harness in the AI they already use (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor) and keep receiving versioned tool modules and the updates that keep them working when the AIs change. The club never spends AI credit on the member's behalf.
- **Ladder** (prices are hypotheses stored as data in `plans`, never in code): free samples → entry kit (one-time, catalog and updates without expiry, 1 device) → subscription (monthly or annual: advanced lessons, recipes, meetings, roadmap vote, 3 devices) → Pro (commercial license, "open the hood" depth, 5 devices) → group mentoring and advisory.
- **Delivery**: the dashboard issues the member token; `npx flyee` installs and updates from the platform's package server. Every update rotates the token; after 30 days without an update the member revalidates in the dashboard, which is where the next tier is offered. Installed tools keep working when access ends; only updates stop.
- **Catalog**: one icon per module, filtered by seven stages (Planejar, Construir, Publicar, Divulgar, Vender, Escalar, Manter). Each module page carries a short lesson in pt-BR and EN (unlisted YouTube), versions, changelog, declared permissions and checksum.
- **Metrics**: usage events only, never content, dimensioned by segment (`produto_proprio`, `freelancer_agencia`, `profissional_ia`, `dev`, `outro`), AI tool and language. The focus segment is chosen by a data rule, not a date.

## Structure

- `apps/web` — Next.js 15 (App Router) + React 19 + MUI v9 + MUI X Premium + Tailwind 4, deployed on Vercel. See `apps/web/CLAUDE.md`.
  - **Member dashboard** (`app/(dashboard)`): `/inicio` (interim home: activation checklist + empty state until phase 5), `/settings` (profile, security and 2FA, connected apps, billing). Phase 5 adds the catalog, recipes, news, meetings, roadmap and devices screens. Screens are goal-first, never CRUD by default; quality is enforced by the `product-screen` skill (loaded by `.claude/hooks/product-screen-guard.mjs`, which also injects `components/product/catalog.json`), the `product-lint` hook and the `product-verify` skill.
  - **Admin** (`app/(dashboard)/admin`, superadmin only): overview, organizations, billing, AI model prices, audit, insights, backups, announcements, help, blog, site and support (launch stage, operating company, support channels). Phase 6 adds catálogo, roadmap, membros, métricas, encontros and leads. Admin copy is hardcoded pt-BR.
  - **Public site** (`app/[locale]/(marketing)`): the waitlist (`/espera`), interim pages (home, `/planos`, `/contato`, `/ajuda`, `/blog`) and the legal pages rendered from `consent_terms`, composed from `components/marketing/*`, in Portuguese at `/` and in English at `/en` with translated addresses (`src/i18n/routing.ts`). Until the launch stage is `open`, every primary CTA leads to the waitlist. Phase 7.2 rebuilds the other pages with the club's copy. Quality is enforced by the `marketing-page` skill (loaded by `.claude/hooks/marketing-guard.mjs`) and the `marketing-lint` hook.
  - **Checkout and auth**: `/assinatura`, `/auth/*`, billing webhooks at `/api/webhooks/[provider]`.
  - **CLI connection and delivery** (`docs/CLI-CONTRACT.md`): the OAuth 2.1 server for the first-party `flyee-cli` client (`/oauth/authorize` with its revalidation variant, `/ativar` for device codes, `/revalidar`, `/api/oauth/{token,device,revoke}`), the delivery API `/api/cli/*` (every call walks `lib/cli/gates.ts`: token → scope → entitlement → device → rate), the package upload `/api/admin/catalog/{uploads,versions}` and the public checksum page `/verificar/[ref]`.
- `packages/design-tokens` — design system source of truth: the provisional palette in `css/green.css`, neutrals in `css/common.css`, `css/marketing.css` (fluid display scale, section rhythm, motion). See its README.
- `packages/db` — the SQL baseline with RLS on every table and explicit grants (one organization per member: the personal workspace), the pgTAP suite, and a Drizzle mirror generated from the migrations. See its README.
- `packages/auth` — Supabase clients (browser/server/middleware/service), 2FA step-up, and the parallel session cookie used by support impersonation.
- `packages/billing` — the ladder (the kit as a one-time access purchase; membership and Pro, monthly and yearly; every plan in BRL and in USD), subscriptions with price snapshots, entitlement grants, coupons, invoices; Asaas (BRL) and Stripe (USD) behind one `PaymentProvider`, routed by the plan's currency. Pure, client-safe helpers in `@flyee/billing/currency` and `@flyee/billing/entitlements`. See `docs/BILLING.md`.
- `packages/email` — Resend + React Email (server-only); no-ops without `RESEND_API_KEY`, so callers keep a fallback.
- `packages/jobs` — Inngest client + typed event map; functions are served by `apps/web` at `/api/inngest`. `sendEvent` never throws; callers fall back to inline work.
- `packages/audit` — append-only `audit_events`, the `access_events` sign-in trail, row versioning, versioned consent terms and acceptances.
- `packages/backup` — nightly logical backups of every `public` table, plus on demand from `/admin/backups`.
- `packages/ai` — chat providers (Anthropic/Gemini/OpenRouter) behind one interface, used by `/admin/insights`; usage feeds the `ai_spend` ledger.
- `packages/fields` — pure validators/formatters/masks (phone, CPF/CNPJ, CEP, currency; persist digits) + the ViaCEP lookup provider.
- `packages/onboarding` — activation state machinery; the steps live in `apps/web/src/lib/onboarding.ts`.
- `packages/content` — `BRAND` (site identity) + the message catalogs `messages/{pt-BR,en}.json`; brand master art in `packages/content/brand/`.
- `packages/catalog` — the `flyee.module.json` manifest schema (zod, published as JSON Schema at `/api/cli/schema/module`) and the catalog's version rules, shared by the upload pipeline and the delivery API.
- `docs/` — `PRODUCT.md`, `PLANO-IMPLEMENTACAO.md`, `DEPLOY.md`, `DESIGN.md` (provisional direction), `ASAAS-GO-LIVE.md`, `BILLING.md` (the billing design), `CLI-CONTRACT.md` (the contract the CLI builds against), `BILLING-AUDIT.md` (historical), `SEO.md` and `TRACKING.md` (rewritten in phase 7).
- `attachments/` — input inbox: drop project material here; agents route each file to its canonical home per `attachments/README.md`.

## Golden rules

- **Platform, not product.** Never add CLI, harness or module logic here. The product exists in this repo only as the `/api/cli/*` contract and the module manifest schema.
- **Configurable data, never constants**: prices, plan limits, device ceilings, rate limits, grace windows, guarantee days and trial lengths live in `plans` and `platform_settings`.
- **Honest metrics**: `product_events` records usage, never content, through one allowlist of names and property values; segment, locale and AI tool are stamped from the profile on the server, never trusted from the client.
- Every mutation records an audit event (`recordAudit` in `apps/web/src/lib/audit.ts`). Every table has RLS, and every new migration states its grants explicitly.
- Visual identity changes ONLY in `packages/design-tokens/css/*.css`; run `npm run tokens:generate` and commit `tokens.generated.ts` with it.
- npm workspaces: install dependencies from the root (`npm install`), never inside an app.
- Icons: Phosphor through the tsconfig alias `@/icons/nexture/*` → `src/icons/phosphor/*` (fallback stubs re-export Nexture).
- Fonts: Mulish (`--font-body`) and Urbanist (`--font-heading`); `font-display` falls back to Urbanist until a licensed display face is chosen and wired as `--font-display` in the root layout.
- Red is reserved for risk and failure.

## Shared Claude/Codex harness

- `CLAUDE.md`, `apps/web/CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/rules/*`, `.claude/skills/*` and `.claude/hooks/*` are the canonical shared sources. They are the platform's development harness: nothing in them is distributed to members. Do not maintain a second hand-written Codex copy.
- Codex reads the generated `AGENTS.md` mirror and the generated `.agents/skills/*` bridges. `.codex/config.toml` points its lifecycle hooks at the same implementations under `.claude/hooks/`.
- `PostToolUse` runs `scripts/sync-agent-harness.mjs` after canonical harness edits. `npm run harness:check` and `npm run harness:test` also run in the pre-commit hook.

## Commands (root)

- `npm run dev` / `build` / `start` / `lint` / `lint:fix` / `prettier` — delegate to `apps/web`.
- `npm run typecheck` — `apps/web` with its pinned TypeScript 5.8. Never run a bare root `npx tsc` on apps/web: it picks the hoisted TS 6.
- `npm run test` — `@flyee/ai` node tests + the web vitest suite. `npm run test:e2e` / `test:a11y` — Playwright against a production build.
- `npm run ci:verify` — everything CI runs: harness checks, MUI class check, typecheck, tests, build.
- `node scripts/prune-messages.mjs --check|--write|--list` — message catalogs without unused or missing keys (pt-BR is the reference).
- `npm run test:db:embedded` — migrations + pgTAP on an embedded PostgreSQL 17, no Docker (first run installs it into `.cache/`). `npm run db:start` / `db:stop` / `test:db` — the same through local Supabase (needs Docker). The `db:*:remote` scripts are gated: see "Safety during the transition".
- `npm run db:schema:pull` — regenerate the Drizzle mirror from the migrations.
- `npm run tokens:generate` — regenerate the TS token mirror.

## Platform decisions

- Deploy: Vercel, only through GitHub Actions (`docs/DEPLOY.md`). Database, auth and storage: Supabase (Postgres + RLS). ORM: Drizzle. Email: Resend. Jobs and cron: Inngest. Billing: Asaas for BRL (PIX, card, Asaas issues the NFS-e) and Stripe for USD, routed by the purchase currency.
- Locales: pt-BR (default) and en, hybrid since phase 7.1: the public site lives under `app/[locale]` with next-intl `pathnames` (pt-BR at `/`, English at `/en` with translated paths, both indexed with hreflang), while dashboard, admin, auth and checkout keep the cookie and profile locale.
- Lessons are unlisted YouTube videos gated by the page and by RLS. Meetings use an external link (Zoom/Meet), with registration and click-through recorded on the platform.
- Do not introduce Cloudflare-specific services (Workers, D1, R2, Workers AI).

This repo stays **private**: the UI layer contains commercially licensed code (MUI X Premium license and the Nexture template components).

===== apps/web/CLAUDE.md =====

# flyee.club web (apps/web)

Next.js 15 (App Router) + React 19 — the only app of the flyee.club platform: public site, member dashboard, checkout, admin consoles and the CLI delivery API. See the root `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/PRODUCT.md` and `docs/PLANO-IMPLEMENTACAO.md`.

> The database is the baseline in `packages/db/migrations` (`0000`–`0018`, plus the migrations added since, described in `packages/db/README.md`). Prefer the function name when searching for a rule.

## Stack and conventions

- **UI**: MUI v9 is the base. Before building a component, look for a MUI or MUI X equivalent (installed: Data Grid + Pro, Charts + Pro, Date Pickers, Tree View, Lab). Icons: **Phosphor** through the `@/icons/nexture/*` tsconfig alias (real adapters plus Nexture fallback stubs, see `src/icons/README.md`); never import an icon library directly.
- **Styling**: MUI theme driven by CSS variables (`hsl(var(--token))`) from `@flyee/design-tokens`. Component overrides live in `src/style/**/*.css` inside CSS layers (`theme, base, mui, components, utilities`). Tailwind 4 for layout utilities, merged with `tailwind-merge`. Run `npm run check:mui-classes` after touching `src/style/**`.
- **Themes**: one locked palette (`theme-green`, provisional) × light/dark, applied as classes on `<html>` by `src/theme/theme-provider.tsx`. Fonts: Mulish (`--font-body`), Urbanist (`--font-heading`); `font-display` falls back to Urbanist.
- **Forms**: Formik + Yup. Semantic data (phone, CPF/CNPJ, CEP, money) uses `components/product/fields/*`, never a raw `TextField`; persist digits, never masks.
- **i18n**: next-intl; every user-facing string goes through messages. Locales `pt-BR` (default) and `en`; catalogs in `packages/content/messages/`. `src/lib/i18n/messages.test.ts` pins key parity, no blank values and identical ICU placeholders. `node scripts/prune-messages.mjs --check` fails on keys no code renders and on keys the code renders that the catalog lacks. Namespaces: `marketing` (public site), `auth`, `product` (member dashboard, billing, settings), `dashboard` (chrome and menu). The home's copy lives in `components/marketing/home-copy/{pt-BR,en}.ts`; `pt-BR.ts` is the structural source of truth (`HomeCopy = typeof homeCopyPtBR`).
- **Admin copy is hardcoded pt-BR**, outside i18n: the operator surface has one reader. Code comments stay in English; a database value (enum, slug, status) is mapped to a label, never shown raw. `components/data-grid/data-table.tsx` takes its grid chrome from MUI X's own locale pack.
- **Which language a request is in** depends on the kind of page, and `i18n/request.ts` is the one place that decides it:
  - **Public site: the URL.** Pages live under `app/[locale]/` (Portuguese at `/`, English at `/en` with translated addresses) and are declared in `src/i18n/routing.ts` (next-intl `pathnames`, `localeDetection: false`). The middleware runs next-intl only for those addresses (`matchPublicPath`), merging the refreshed Supabase cookies into its rewrite, and persists the URL language in the locale cookie so sign-in and the app that follow continue in it. Internal links use `LocaleLink`/`localizeHref` with the Portuguese path; `app/[locale]/layout.tsx` repeats the `NextIntlClientProvider` because the root layout is not re-rendered by a client-side navigation; the public language switch is a full page load. A browser that reads the other language gets an offer (`language-suggestion.tsx`), never a redirect.
  - **Everything else (sign-in, member area, checkout, admin): the visitor.** `lib/locale-request.ts` (`resolveRequestLocale`): the cookie is the visitor's choice and always wins; otherwise `lib/locale-detection.ts` decides from `Accept-Language`, then Vercel's `x-vercel-ip-country`. Three rules are load-bearing: detection happens at RENDER time, not only in the middleware (a cookie set by the middleware lands on the response); a crawler is never switched (`isCrawler`); an automatic switch is always announced (`COOKIE_KEYS.localeAuto`). The in-app switch (`setClientLocale` in `i18n/locale.ts`) also writes `profiles.locale` through `update_member_profile`, outside support sessions; a new browser does not read the profile yet (detection decides until the member switches).
- **Path alias**: `@/*` → `./src/*`. **Brand**: identity comes from `@flyee/content` (`src/brand.ts` re-exports it); the logo is the single component `src/components/logo/logo.tsx`.
- **Remote data**: `lib/remote-state.ts` (`RemoteState<T>`: idle, loading, success, empty, error). An error is never rendered as empty.

## Member dashboard (product layer)

- Routes: `/inicio` (`DEFAULTS.appRoot`; interim home with the activation checklist and an empty state), `/settings` (profile and avatar, credentials), `/settings/security` (2FA, sign-in history), `/settings/connections` (OAuth clients holding a live token, with revoke; becomes `/settings/devices` in phase 5), `/settings/billing`. Phase 5 adds `/modulos`, `/receitas`, `/novidades`, `/encontros`, `/roadmap`, `/settings/devices` and the onboarding wizard; the dashboard catalog is `/modulos` because the public one is `/catalogo`.
- **Activation** (`lib/onboarding.ts`): four steps with LIVE predicates, never click tracking — profile (segment, AI tool, language) → access (kit or plan) → install (`npx flyee login`) → first run (closed by the CLI's first `tool.executed`). The facts come from the definer RPC `member_activation_facts()` (phase 2); until it exists every fact reads false. `isActivated` = a device AND a first execution. `resolvePostAuthDestination` is called by sign-in, sign-up, `/auth/callback` and `/auth/two-factor`; never put that check in the middleware.
- **Entitlements**: `hooks/use-entitlements.ts` calls `org_entitlements(org)`, the single answer to what a workspace may use: the free floor, live grants (the kit, licenses, courtesies), the live subscription with its add-ons, and an unconfirmed PIX inside its window, merged so more sources never mean fewer rights, with the tier and the sources named. Screens branch on it, never on plan names. `org_has_entitlement(org, key)` is the yes/no form for policies and gates. `components/product/gate-notice.tsx` renders the gate states (`available`, `loading`, `unknown` with retry, `blocked` with a reason). `components/layout/menu/plan-indicator.tsx` shows the tier and the upgrade path.
- **Sign-up**: one person is one account. `handle_new_user` creates the profile AND the personal workspace from `display_name`; the sign-up metadata also carries `locale` (the phase 2 trigger reads `display_name`, `segment`, `ai_tool`, `locale`). `/auth/complete-profile` is only the safety net for an account without a workspace.
- **Usage events**: the browser reports only offers shown and clicked (`trackOffer` in `lib/product-events.ts`, which terminates the PostgREST builder with `.then()`: a bare `void supabase.rpc(...)` never sends the request). Everything that counts toward a metric is written by the backend with `trackServerEvent` (`lib/product-events-server.ts`). The database stamps segment, language and AI tool from the profile and drops any property outside its allowlist.
- Reusable blocks live in `components/product/*` and are listed in `components/product/catalog.json` (injected by the `product-screen-guard` hook). Every zero-data view uses `EmptyState`.

## Public site (marketing layer)

- Routes in `src/app/[locale]/(marketing)/`, each in Portuguese and English: home `/` and `/en`, `/planos` (`/en/pricing`), `/contato` (`/en/contact`), `/ajuda` (`/en/help`), `/blog` (`/en/blog`), `/legal/{termos,privacidade,cookies}` (`/en/legal/{terms,privacy,cookies}`). Phase 7.2 adds `/como-funciona`, `/catalogo`, `/sobre`, `/espera`, `/verificar/[ref]` and the founders page, whose addresses are already declared in `src/i18n/routing.ts`. A new public page is declared there (both addresses; that is also what makes it public to the middleware), enters `src/app/sitemap.ts` when indexed (once per language, with alternates), and spreads `publicPageMetadata({ path, locale })` from `lib/seo.ts` into its `generateMetadata` (canonical, hreflang with `x-default`, Open Graph URL).
- ONE design system: pages compose the primitives in `src/components/marketing/` (`Section`/`Container`/`SectionHeader`, Hero, FeatureRows, BentoGrid, StatBand, PricingSection, Faq, Cta), listed in `components/marketing/catalog.json`. The inherited Landing DS is gone. `docs/DESIGN.md` holds the provisional direction; phase 7.3 rewrites it.
- `/ajuda` and `/blog` render DB-managed content (written in `/admin/help` and `/admin/blog`) through `src/lib/public-content.ts` (anon client, published rows, only in the language of the address: translations are rows linked by `translation_group`, and a slug of the other language redirects to its translation or to the section index); Markdown renders via `components/marketing/markdown-prose.tsx` (raw HTML ignored).
- **Legal pages render `consent_terms`** (`components/marketing/legal-document.tsx` over `lib/legal.ts`): the version in force of `terms`, `privacy` and `cookies` in the language of the address, with version and date, so the page shows exactly the text people accept. When the text cannot be read the page says so; the catalogs hold no second copy of the terms.
- **Launch stage** (`lib/launch.ts`, `platform_settings.launch`, migration 0019): in `waitlist` (the seed, and the fallback for anything unreadable) every primary CTA of the public site leads to `/espera`; in `open` they lead to sign-up and checkout. Sign-in and sign-up stay reachable in both. The superadmin flips it at `/admin/support`, which also holds the operating company printed in the footer (`legal_entity`, read by `getLegalEntity`): the terms identify the operator "in the site footer".
- **Waitlist** (`/espera`, `/en/waitlist`): `espera/actions.ts` validates (honeypot, consent), calls `submit_lead` with the service role (first-touch campaign from the attribution cookie, network window keyed by an HMAC of the IP with `PUBLIC_FORMS_IP_SALT`), and e-mails the double opt-in link (`sendLeadConfirmationEmail`, in the language the address signed up in). The answer never reveals whether an address was already listed. The link `/espera/confirmar?t=` is rewritten by the middleware: the token moves into an httpOnly cookie (`COOKIE_KEYS.leadConfirm`) and the page loads at the clean address, because analytics scripts and Referer headers carry URLs; confirming takes a button press, because mail scanners open every link. `lib/lead-jobs.ts` runs `purge_expired_leads` daily (unconfirmed addresses go after 7 days, as the page promises).
- Pricing reads plans through `@flyee/billing/public` (`listPublicPlans`, read-only) with i18n placeholder plans as fallback; the contact form sends through `@flyee/email` (`CONTACT_FORM_TO`).
- Display type: `font-display text-display-{2xl,xl,lg,md}` (fluid clamp scale from `@flyee/design-tokens/css/marketing.css`). Motion: GSAP only inside marketing client components via `<Reveal>`/`useGSAP` (transforms + `autoAlpha`, honors `prefers-reduced-motion`); never in admin code.
- Tracking: the marketing layout renders Meta Pixel and GA4 server-side (opt-out through the cookie notice, `lib/analytics.ts`); sign-up and purchase conversions go server-side (`lib/meta-capi.ts`, `lib/ga4-mp.ts`). `docs/TRACKING.md` is rewritten in phase 7.3.

## Billing and checkout

- `/settings/billing` (the ladder in the member's currency, current subscription, cancel with a reason and undo, invoices, billing profile, pending checkout, payment recovery) and `/assinatura?plan=<slug>` (the focused checkout; without `plan` it opens the kit in the visitor's currency; Pix, card or installments in BRL, Stripe Checkout in USD). Server actions in `settings/billing/actions.ts` (checkouts), `actions-cancel.ts` and `actions-recovery.ts`, sharing `billing-server.ts`; provider webhooks at `api/webhooks/[provider]/route.ts`, idempotent through `claim_billing_webhook_event`/`complete_billing_webhook_event` with an attempt ceiling.
- **Dunning grace**: `past_due` keeps access for a configurable window (`platform_settings` key `dunning`) counted from `subscriptions.past_due_since`; `billing_past_due_grace_ends()` is the one answer every gate shares. Installed tools always keep working; only updates stop.
- **Comped plans**: `set_org_plan(org, plan, note)` puts a workspace on a tier without checkout (betas, partners, the team). It updates the live row instead of inserting, keeps the period bounds NULL, refuses a provider-backed subscription (`provider_managed`) and stamps `self_grant` in the audit event when the operator comps their own account.
- The founders offer counts real seats (`lib/founders-offer.ts`); the guarantee window comes from `platform_settings` (`lib/guarantee.ts`); a pending PIX survives a closed tab (`lib/pending-pix.ts`).
- **Entitlements**: `org_entitlements(org)` is the one answer (free floor + live grants + live subscription + add-ons, with `tier` and `sources`). Screens read it through `hooks/use-entitlements.ts` and `@flyee/billing/entitlements`, never by plan name or slug. The kit is an `entitlement_grants` row the webhook creates on the paid invoice; CLI tokens are revoked only when catalog access really ends (`lib/billing-lifecycle.ts`).
- **Currency**: `?moeda=` (kept in a cookie by the middleware) or the page language picks BRL or USD (`lib/billing-currency.ts`), and the plan's currency picks the provider. A yearly BRL plan split into installments is ONE purchase that does not renew. Full design, state machine, refunds and deferred items: `docs/BILLING.md`.

## Platform admin and account

- Superadmin area at `src/app/(dashboard)/admin`: `layout.tsx` is a server gate on `profiles.is_superadmin` (RLS stays the real defense); the Admin menu group renders only for superadmins (`hooks/use-is-superadmin.ts`). Consoles: `/admin` (metrics via `admin_metrics()`), `/admin/organizations` (accounts and people; ban, 2FA state and reset need `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`), `/admin/billing`, `/admin/ai` (model price book), `/admin/audit` (audit trail + sign-in log), `/admin/insights`, `/admin/backups`, `/admin/announcements`, `/admin/help`, `/admin/blog`, `/admin/support`. The accounts view and dossier still carry the inherited fields; phase 6 rewrites them as `admin_members_overview()`/`admin_member_dossier()`.
- Every mutation records an audit event through `lib/audit.ts` (`recordAudit`). Sign-ins are logged by a database trigger; members see their own in `/settings/security`.
- **Granting the superadmin role** (`set_user_superadmin(user, value, note)`): the flag is fenced by a trigger on `profiles` keyed on WHO is asking (`is_superadmin()` reads the database), because a self-`PATCH` of `is_superadmin` would otherwise promote any signed-in user. Self-change is refused in both directions. A session with no JWT (service role, migration, psql) passes: that is how the first superadmin is made.
- **Support impersonation** (`lib/impersonation-actions.ts`, started from `/admin/organizations`): the operator works inside a member's account through a **parallel session cookie** (`@flyee/auth` `authCookieName`), so leaving deletes a cookie and never strands the operator. Load-bearing: the write fence is in the DATABASE (`is_impersonated()` matches the JWT `session_id` against `impersonation_sessions`; triggers refuse member-owned writes), and it never expires; ending a visit uses `signOut({ scope: "local" })`, never the global default; starting requires the operator's own session at AAL2; credentials and `/admin` are blocked in the middleware. A reason is required, the member is notified, and the access is labelled as support in their sign-in history. Duration lives in `platform_settings` (`impersonation`).
- **Account deletion** (`delete-account-dialog.tsx`, server action `deleteAccount`, RPC `admin_delete_account(user, confirm_email, reason)`): the unit is the account plus every workspace it alone belongs to. The order is fixed: re-read the preview, cancel any live provider subscription (a failure deletes nothing), run the RPC in one transaction (it deletes rows that hold data through NO ACTION/RESTRICT references first, holder before held, and purges `record_versions`), then remove storage files through the Storage API using `admin_orphaned_account_storage`, which refuses anything still alive. Refused in the database: yourself, any superadmin, a support session, a live provider subscription. The audit event `admin.account.deleted` survives with counts only.
- **AI spend** (`lib/ai-spend.ts`, price book at `/admin/ai`): every provider call records one `ai_spend` row through the `ChatProvider` `onUsage` sink. Prices are configuration (`platform_settings` key `ai_prices`, per million tokens), shipped empty; an unpriced model reports `priced = false`, and consoles show the unpriced count beside every total. Cost is stored in USD micros and converted only with an operator-set rate.
- `/admin/insights` (`api/admin/insights/route.ts`): the model writes SQL from an `information_schema` catalog and each statement runs inside a `read only` transaction with a 5 s `statement_timeout`. **The read-only transaction is the safety boundary, not the prompt.** Every executed query is audited and shown. Needs `DATABASE_URL` and one AI provider key.
- **Daily operator watch** (`lib/admin-jobs.ts`, Inngest cron): one bell notification and one e-mail per superadmin, only when there is something to report; `notifications.source_key` makes the whole digest idempotent per day. Phase 6 replaces it with the weekly segment digest.
- `/admin/backups` (`@flyee/backup`): nightly cron plus "Run backup now" (inline fallback without Inngest). Archives land in the private `backups` bucket; downloads are signed URLs.
- Account plumbing is real: the header bell reads `notifications` (create rows server-side with `lib/notifications.ts`), announcements render in the dashboard layout with per-user dismissal, `/settings` edits the profile (avatar in the `avatars` bucket) and credentials. The quick-support widget (`components/support/support-widget.tsx`) reads the channels from `platform_settings` (`support`, edited at `/admin/support`), falls back to `BRAND.support`, and renders nothing until a human channel exists.

## Auth

- Supabase through `@flyee/auth` (`client`/`server`/`middleware`/`service`). `src/middleware.ts` refreshes the session and protects everything except the public pages (`matchPublicPath`, from `src/i18n/routing.ts`) and `PUBLIC_PREFIXES`. Without `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`/`NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` the middleware no-ops and the auth screens show a configuration hint.
- 2FA (TOTP): enrolled at `/settings/security`; the middleware forces the AAL2 step-up at `/auth/two-factor`.
- Internal redirects go through `lib/safe-next.ts` (`sanitizeInternalNext`), never a raw `next` parameter.
- **CLI token server** (`lib/oauth/*`, `docs/CLI-CONTRACT.md`): one first-party public client, `flyee-cli`, seeded in migration 0010; no dynamic registration. Browser login with PKCE and a loopback redirect on any port (`lib/oauth/redirect.ts`), device authorization (`/api/oauth/device` + `/ativar`, `lib/oauth/device-code.ts`), revocation (`/api/oauth/revoke`). Opaque tokens, one family per machine (`device_id`), access 1 h, refresh 30 days rotated on every use: an expired refresh answers `invalid_grant` with `error_uri` = `/revalidar`, and a login on a machine that held a chain before renders the revalidation screen. Logins, revalidations and expired refreshes are product events (`cli.login`, `token.revalidated`, `update.denied_token_expired`).
- **Delivery API** (`app/api/cli/*`): every handler runs inside `runCliRequest` (`lib/cli/gates.ts`), which checks token → scope → `org_entitlements` (read on every call) → `X-Flyee-Device` → `cli_rate_allowance`, answers refusals as `{ error, message (member's language, lib/cli/messages.ts), action_url }` and files each call in `cli_requests`. Downloads are 300-second signed URLs from the private `modules` bucket; the CLI verifies size and SHA-256. Catalog reads live in `lib/cli/catalog.ts`.
- **Packages**: `lib/catalog/package.ts` inspects a ZIP (safe paths, size ceilings, manifest `files` equal to the archive); `lib/catalog/upload.ts` turns a staged upload into a draft version; `lib/catalog/version-actions.ts` publishes, marks stable and yanks (superadmin, audited).

## Commands (run from the monorepo root)

- `npm run dev` — dev server. `npm run build` — production build. `npm run typecheck` — TypeScript 5.8 pinned to this app.
- `npm run test:web` — vitest. `npm run test:e2e` / `npm run test:a11y` — Playwright against a production build (`e2e/baseline.spec.ts`).
- `npm run lint:fix` / `npm run prettier` — lint and formatting.

## Watch out

- `src/style/global.css` imports tokens from `@flyee/design-tokens/css/*`; never recreate tokens locally.
- Deploys go ONLY through GitHub Actions (`.github/workflows/deploy.yml`: `vercel pull/build/deploy --prebuilt`); the Vercel Git integration stays disconnected. Runbook: `docs/DEPLOY.md`.
- Server-only secrets (`DATABASE_URL`, `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`, provider keys) never reach client components.
- `apps/web/.env` holds inherited MedChina production credentials and `apps/web/.env.local` blanks them; keep `.env.local` until the flyee.club services exist (root `CLAUDE.md`, "Safety during the transition").

# Product (authenticated app) UX

- The `product-screen` skill is MANDATORY for any create/edit here — a `PreToolUse` hook (`.claude/hooks/product-screen-guard.mjs`) loads it automatically; you never wait to be asked.
- **Goal, not table**: design from the user's job and what success looks like. Never default to a CRUD table of rows — that shape is allowed only when the job really is scan/compare/manage many rows.
- **Never a blank screen**: every zero-data view uses `EmptyState` (icon + why + the ONE next action). A brand-new user must find a path to value (the aha moment).
- Long setups use `SetupWizard` (progressive disclosure); steps to first result use `OnboardingChecklist` + `@flyee/onboarding` (state only; step definitions live in the project's code).
- **Engagement**: completion drive (`ActivationProgress`) and competence feedback only. Never ship points, badges, leaderboards or streaks — documented failures, and streaks carry regulatory risk.
- MUI v9 + theme tokens only, next-intl for every string, inline form errors near the field, skeletons that reserve space.
- **Semantic fields**: phone, CPF/CNPJ, CEP and money never go in a raw `TextField` — use `components/product/fields/*` (mask + check-digit validation + CEP auto-fill via `@flyee/fields`); persist `onlyDigits()`, never the masked string.

# Design tokens

- `packages/design-tokens/css/*.css` is the source of truth for visual identity. `src/tokens.generated.ts` is GENERATED — never edit it manually.
- After any change in `css/*.css`, run `npm run tokens:generate` at the root and include the generated file in the same commit.
- Color values are bare HSL triplets (`191 100% 46%`), consumed via `hsl(var(--token))` in CSS. Keep this format; do not introduce hex/rgb.
- Every color token must exist in light/dark pairs (`:root`/`.dark` in common, `.theme-x`/`.theme-x.dark` in theme files).

# Icon contract

- Pages import icons only as `@/icons/nexture/ni-*` (the alias may be remapped per project to an adapter set — see `apps/web/src/icons/README.md`). Never import an icon library (Phosphor, Lucide, MUI icons for decoration) directly in a page.
- Every icon component implements `NextureIconsProps` (`size`, `variant`, `className`, `oneTone`) and is a default export.
- Alternative sets live in sibling folders (`src/icons/phosphor/`, ...) with identical file names; gaps are filled by `npm run icons:stubs -w @flyee/web` (fallback re-exports, never overwritten).
- Adapters import icon libs from their SSR-safe entry (e.g. `@phosphor-icons/react/dist/ssr`) so they work in Server Components.

===== .claude/rules/marketing.md =====

# Marketing layer boundaries

- **One design system.** Every public page (the home, the institutional pages and the campaign pages in `app/[locale]/(funil)/`) composes the primitives in `apps/web/src/components/marketing/`: `Section`/`Container`/`SectionHeader` plus the archetypes listed in `catalog.json`. Never hand-tuned per-page spacing or widths, never a parallel stylesheet vocabulary. The inherited MedChina "Landing DS" was removed on 2026-09-30.
- The `marketing-page` skill is MANDATORY for any create/edit/add-section under `app/[locale]/(marketing)`, `app/[locale]/(funil)` or `components/marketing`. The `PreToolUse` hook (`.claude/hooks/marketing-guard.mjs`) loads it automatically for `(marketing)` and `components/marketing`; in `(funil)` load it yourself, you never wait to be asked.
- The committed visual direction lives in `docs/DESIGN.md` and is STRICT: new pages, edits and new sections INHERIT it. Never re-run the direction engine or restyle the UI unless the user explicitly asks for a "redesign". Adding a section triggers a whole-page coherence pass so all sections stay aesthetically aligned.
- **Locales are in the path** (phase 7.1): Portuguese at the root (`/planos`), English under `/en` with translated addresses (`/en/pricing`). Every public page lives under `app/[locale]/` in a folder named after its Portuguese (internal) path, and is declared in `apps/web/src/i18n/routing.ts` (`pathnames`) with both addresses. That declaration is also what makes the middleware treat it as public: there is no separate list of public pages. Only the public site is routed this way; sign-in, the member area, checkout and the admin keep the visitor's cookie/profile language and have no locale in the URL.
- Internal links on public surfaces go through `LocaleLink` (`components/marketing/locale-link.tsx`, also as MUI's `LinkComponent`) or `localizeHref`: `href` is the internal Portuguese path, the link renders the address of the language being read. Links to `/auth/*` and other non-public routes pass through unchanged.
- An INDEXED page also goes to `apps/web/src/app/sitemap.ts`, which emits it once per language with hreflang alternates. A `noindex` page (the campaign pages in `(funil)`, `/fundadores`, `/verificar/[ref]`) stays out of the sitemap and is named in its exclusion comment. Indexing is decided by `metadata` + `sitemap.ts`, never by the route group.
- `/ajuda` and `/blog` are DB-managed: content is written in `/admin/help` / `/admin/blog` and fetched through `apps/web/src/lib/public-content.ts` (anon client, published rows). An address in a language serves content written in that language, never a fallback; translations are separate rows linked by `translation_group`, each with its own slug. Markdown renders via `components/marketing/markdown-prose.tsx`. Never interpolate DB content as raw HTML.
- SEO is part of every page, per `docs/SEO.md`: exactly one `<h1>` (the page title: `SectionHeader as="h1"` / `PricingSection headingAs="h1"` when the lead is not a `<Hero>`), a localized title + description via `generateMetadata` that spreads `publicPageMetadata({ path, locale })` from `lib/seo.ts` (canonical, hreflang with `x-default`, Open Graph URL and locale), and structured data through `<JsonLd>` (`components/marketing/json-ld.tsx`), never a hand-written `<script>`. `Organization`/`FAQPage`/`Product` schemas are already emitted by the layout/`Faq`/`PricingSection`; do not duplicate them.
- Marketing copy lives in the `marketing` i18n namespace, in BOTH locale files (`pt-BR`, `en`), campaign pages included. No hardcoded strings. The home's structured copy lives in `components/marketing/home-copy/{pt-BR,en}.ts`, with `pt-BR.ts` as the structural source of truth (TypeScript refuses the build when `en.ts` drifts). Emphasis is inline (`**em**`, `__strong__`, `==mark==`, `\n`), rendered by `home-copy/rich.tsx`; never put JSX in a copy file.
- **Blocking on every public page**: exactly one `<h1>`, real `alt` text, no fabricated testimonials, metrics or logos, prices and limits read from data (`plans`), honest scarcity (any counter or deadline derives from server state, such as `founders_offer()`), and no claim that the club spends AI credit on the member's behalf.
- GSAP only inside marketing client components (`Reveal`/`useGSAP`), transforms + `autoAlpha` only, honoring `prefers-reduced-motion`. Never import GSAP in admin code.
- Site identity (name, tagline, siteUrl, favicons) comes from `apps/web/src/brand.ts`; the logo is the single component `components/logo/logo.tsx`.

# apps/web boundaries

- `apps/web` is the only app in this repo. Code shared between the app and tooling lives in `packages/*`.
- Do not redefine theme tokens locally (`--primary`, `--grey-*` etc.) — they come from `@flyee/design-tokens`.
- This repo is the flyee.club PLATFORM. The product (the `npx flyee` CLI, the harness core, the module contents) is a separate project: here, it only exists as the API contract (`/api/cli/*`) and the module manifest schema it consumes. Never add product logic to this repo.
